verification_report.summary:
The complete supplied proof is correct under the stated accepted inputs. All deductions were checked in textual order. The coordinate loci, interpreted inside C^n minus the origin, descend to smooth connected compact submanifolds. Each coordinate inclusion is a prime Cartier divisor, and any reduced point on the final smooth curve is a prime Cartier divisor. The final curve is C*/<e^-1>, identified by logarithms with C/(Z+2pi i Z), so it is elliptic. The bounded weighted definition at weight zero gives W_m=mathcal W_m(0), because smooth section norms are bounded on compact X_n.

The valuation computation respects the residual line bundles. On Y_(i-1), z_i is a section of L_1 with divisor Y_i; dividing by z_i^a_i therefore implements the required negative divisor twist. At each stage, taking the least exponent and restricting leaves a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree km minus the accumulated exponents. After n-1 steps this is c z_n^r, where c is nonzero and r=km-sum a_i is nonnegative. It is an equivariant, nowhere-vanishing section of the residual bundle L_r on the elliptic curve. Thus its vanishing order is zero at every p, including when r=0; it need not be an invariant scalar function on the quotient. Conversely, each displayed monomial has exactly the asserted valuation, proving equality of valuation sets.

Every normalized valuation lies in the stated simplex, and its vertices occur in degree one, proving equality with the closed convex hull. Containment in x_n=0 gives zero ambient n-dimensional volume. For k>0, the coordinate basis is orthonormal and generates the hyperplane lattice, so its covolume is one and the simplex volume is k^(n-1)/(n-1)!. There is no hidden lattice index or degree periodicity: degree one contains valuations zero and e_i, using z_n^k and z_i z_n^(k-1). The exact count gives dim W_m/m^(n-1)=product from j=1 to n-1 of (k+j/m), divided by (n-1)!, which converges to that same volume.

For k=0, all valuations are zero, the body is a point, and dim W_m=1. The positive-dimensional intrinsic-volume assertion is explicitly restricted to k>0. For n=2, the body is a segment of length k and dim W_m=km+1, including the constant case. The n=3 illustration correctly gives area k^2/2 and zero ambient volume. The final comparison uses the accepted degree 4k and unbounded upper Hermitian mass only in dimension three. Internal definitions and references match their applications; no new external-paper theorem is required. No BMP hypothesis or unaccepted finding from flag_bodies_01 enters the argument. The book was kept read-only. No critical errors or gaps were found.
